name: Albanian nationalism
summary: Albanian nationalism holds that Albanians form one nation defined by language, descent and shared history (Illyrian origins, Skanderbeg), whatever their Muslim, Catholic or Orthodox faith. It grew from the nineteenth-century Rilindja into the 1912 independence and, in Kosovo, the struggle against Yugoslav and Serbian rule. Today it ranges from cultural unity and Euro-Atlantic integration to Pan-Albanian calls for unification.
scope: The mainstream strand from the Rilindja (Frashëri brothers, League of Prizren, 1912 independence) through to current Albanian and Kosovar nationalism including Vetëvendosje's Pan-Albanianism. Excludes Hoxha-era Marxist-Leninist nationalism as a model and the militant Greater Albania fringe. Social and economic answers are mostly inferred because the movement spans left and right parties.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nationalism itself is silent on health policy; Vetëvendosje, the leading nationalist party in Kosovo, proposes health insurance, and Albanian voters broadly expect public provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from Vetëvendosje's labour agenda (severance pay, 40-hour week); the nationalist core says nothing on wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents split: Berisha-style right nationalists favour markets while Vetëvendosje favours a developmental state.

public-ownership.rationale: Vetëvendosje backs state ownership of key industries, but right-wing Albanian nationalists privatised; no shared position.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Progressive taxation appears in Vetëvendosje's programme but the movement as a whole has no economic doctrine.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalism is not tied to a labour position; adherents are spread across left and right parties.

property-fundamental.rationale: Early Rilindja nationalism was shaped by economic liberalism, so private property is mildly favoured, though not a stated principle.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No source ties Albanian nationalism to corporate regulation; left and right nationalists differ.

cut-welfare.rationale: Nationalists on the left run welfare-state programmes and the right does not campaign on cuts; inferred mild disagreement.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not part of the nationalist tradition; Vetëvendosje's social-democratic programme proposes state, not worker, ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented position; security concerns about Serbia and Islamist extremism pull one way, civil liberties the other.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative, family-centred national culture; no source addresses it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists often resist limits on speech but support laws against ethnic incitement in Kosovo.

strong-leader.rationale: Hoxha and Zog built nationalism through strong rule, while Rugova and Kurti represent civic, parliamentary leaders.

state-harmful.rationale: Albanian nationalism is the project of building and defending an Albanian state, from the 1912 independence declaration to Kosovo's statehood.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun culture and the KLA legacy sit against EU-driven regulation; no stated nationalist position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Kosovo's nationalist governments have raised military spending and considered conscription, but the wider movement has no stated position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from socially conservative national culture; the sources do not address it.

decide-locally.rationale: Nationalism seeks a unified national state, and Kosovo's Albanian parties resist devolving power to Serb-majority municipalities.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented nationalist position on penal policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Albanian national identity draws on kinship and customary tradition, but the sources do not state a family doctrine; Vetëvendosje is more liberal.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Albanian nationalist opinion is mostly conservative here, though Vetëvendosje is pro-European and more liberal; no stated programme.

abortion-legal.rationale: Both countries legalised abortion under communism or since; nationalists are not defined by a stance.

more-religion-public.rationale: Albanianism deliberately defined the nation above Muslim, Catholic and Orthodox divisions and kept religion out of public identity.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue the movement addresses; nearest analogue is its demand for redress for Albanian suffering under Yugoslav rule.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from conservative cultural currents; not addressed in sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Rilindja was a movement to build Albanian language, schools, folklore and the Skanderbeg heritage as the basis of the nation.

gradual-change.rationale: Rilindja moderates sought gradual autonomy while later nationalists chose revolt in 1910-12 and the KLA fought in the 1990s.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Albania and Kosovo are emigration countries; immigration is not a nationalist theme in the sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Albanians in Albania and Kosovo see the EU, NATO and the US as the route to security and development, though the UN's handling of Kosovo is resented.

free-trade.rationale: Pro-EU orientation implies openness to trade; the sources give no explicit doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Albanian nationalism puts the nation's interests first yet is strongly Euro-Atlantic and cooperative, so adherents are split on the framing.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Kosovo Albanians owe their liberation to NATO's 1999 intervention, so the idea is central to the movement's recent experience.

open-borders.rationale: The movement seeks Albanian unity across borders but within a state system, not eventually open borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Nothing ties nationalism to degrowth; developmental goals dominate in both countries.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; Vetëvendosje opposes a coal plant but the movement holds no climate doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nationalists cheer the 1910-12 uprisings, the independence rising and the KLA's armed struggle as legitimate resistance to foreign rule.

central-planning.rationale: Hoxha's planned economy is a discredited legacy; most nationalists reject it, though his nationalism is claimed by some.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not part of nationalist doctrine; left nationalists may accept it, right nationalists not.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Vetëvendosje favours import substitution and export promotion, but pro-EU nationalists favour open trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Vetëvendosje proposes a development bank and sovereign fund, while other nationalist parties do not.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marxist abolition was never part of Albanian nationalism; inferred from its national-state focus.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; Vetëvendosje's common currency with Albania implies central institutions are accepted.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No nationalist source supports state-recognised bargaining bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Hoxha's one-party nationalism is remembered as repression, and mainstream Albanian nationalists in Kosovo built multiparty politics, as with Rugova's LDK.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Zog's monarchy used nationalism and the 1913 powers recognised a hereditary principality, but modern nationalists are republicans and a monarchist minority remains.

democracy-best.rationale: Albanian nationalists in Kosovo pursued independence through elections and parallel institutions, and Vetëvendosje stresses democracy and checks and balances.

direct-votes.rationale: Vetëvendosje has called for a unification referendum, but no general stance is documented.

workers-councils.rationale: Foreign to the tradition; inferred from its state-building focus.

right-to-secede.rationale: Kosovo Albanians claimed self-determination and secession from Serbia, yet nationalists oppose Serb or Macedonian separatism within Albanian-held areas.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement drew on popular mobilisation rather than rule by a natural elite; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The KLA and the 1912 rising are honoured, though Rugova's nonviolent resistance was also mainstream.

war-builds-character.rationale: Skanderbeg and Jashari myths glorify fighting, but no source states war builds character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Sami Frashëri envisioned religion separated from the state with each faith led by its own head, and Albanianism sought a faith-neutral nation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Nationalists made the movement secular to unify Muslims, Catholics and Orthodox, so scripture-based law contradicts that aim.

military-superiority.rationale: Kosovo's nationalist government raised military spending, but the movement does not claim superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Albanian nationalism defines the nation by language and descent across states, yet Kosovo's constitution is multiethnic, so adherents are not uniform.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hoxha's Marxism adapted nationalism, but the movement's history centres on the national struggle.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Illyrian descent claims make Albanians the indigenous people, an argument used for Kosovo; not a stated generalisation.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Albanians saw themselves as subjects of Ottoman, not overseas colonial, rule, so no position is inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Albanianism explicitly stood above religion, and Catholic and Orthodox Albanians fear uniting with Muslim-majority networks, so religion-based union is not endorsed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Customary kinship ties and the nation's claims feature in the tradition, but no stated doctrine.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalist concern for the size of the Albanian population in contested areas implies disfavour; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: No source; nationalism sought national development.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No documented position; inferred from conventional democratic orientation.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rilindja looked to Skanderbeg for inspiration but aimed at a modern state, so adherents split.

direct-action.rationale: Albanian nationalist movements have mixed parliamentary and extra-parliamentary action, including Vetëvendosje's street protests.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Entirely foreign to a modernising national movement; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist goal not held by the nationalist mainstream.

production-for-use.rationale: Not part of nationalist doctrine, though the left nationalist party values social needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim; not held by the nationalist mainstream.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Hoxha's regime claimed this, and its legacy is widely rejected among modern Albanian nationalists.

collective-farming.rationale: Hoxha's collectivisation is remembered negatively; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not part of the nationalist account of Balkan conflict, which blames Serb, Greek and Ottoman policy.

taxation-theft.rationale: Nationalism is a state-building project and Vetëvendosje supports progressive taxation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Albanians campaign for collective national rights such as self-determination and Albanian-language education.

conscription.rationale: Vetëvendosje's Kosovo government has considered mandatory conscription and Albania historically conscripted.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalists stress staying and claiming rights where Albanians live, though diaspora emigration is large.

state-as-business.rationale: No source; inferred from the movement's civic-national conception of the state.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Albanian nationalism claims ethnic descent but does not make racial ability claims in the sources.

organic-representation.rationale: The movement uses electoral party politics.

total-state.rationale: Hoxha's totalitarian state is rejected today by mainstream nationalists.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Rilindja (National Awakening) is itself a project of national revival and cultural renewal.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Clan loyalty existed in northern customary law, but nationalism rests on national, not lord-follower, authority.

bound-labor.rationale: Foreign to a modern national movement.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nationalist history uses Illyrian and Skanderbeg narratives as truths, not as power-laden constructs.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No stated position, though Albanian nationalists often cite sympathy for national self-determination and Albania's WWII record of sheltering Jews.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Albanian nationalism treats diaspora and Albanians abroad as part of the nation, with governments creating policies toward the diaspora.

revive-national-language.rationale: The Rilindja created a standard alphabet and schools to make Albanian the language of education, rather than reviving a dead one.

rule-by-example.rationale: No source; inferred from a modern state-law orientation.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement is defined by the claim that Albanians have the right to their own state, as in the 1912 declaration of independence and Kosovo's drive for independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Kosovo's NATO intervention had no UN authorisation and Albanians honour it; not otherwise stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; Albania and Kosovo have little immigration.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism claims unity of the nation across classes; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Albanian nationalism cultivates heritage, though Hoxha destroyed religious buildings; adherents condemn that today.

workers-nation.rationale: Albanian nationalism organises the nation rather than the working class, though left nationalists use class politics too.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: No stated programme; modern nationalist parties support gender equality laws.

ban-interest.rationale: No source; Albanian nationalism is not an Islamic economic movement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Albanian nationalists campaigned against ethnic discrimination of Albanians under Yugoslavia and do not favour segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim; nationalist mainstream does not hold it.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Vetëvendosje opposes the Kosova C coal plant, while others support domestic energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Albanian states have few immigrants; Hoxha assimilated minorities by name changes but today's nationalists have no position.

elite-replacement.rationale: A Western far-right theory not found in Albanian nationalism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Kosovo uses list-proportional representation and Albania uses a regional list system, so adherents work under it; not a nationalist principle.

national-mission.rationale: Albanian nationalism seeks unity and recognition rather than spreading a system abroad.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Vetëvendosje's justice-state pillar centres on anti-corruption, and Albanian voters link EU integration to fixing crime and weak governance.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No source; foreign to the tradition.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nationalist parties of left and right run a developmental or welfare role for the state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of the nationalist programme in the sources.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Albanian nationalists demand equal rights for Albanians in Serbia and Macedonia, and Frashëri's vision gave all faiths freedom to worship.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Hoxha built socialism in one country but modern nationalists do not discuss it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No documented position; Albanian nationalists generally frame Serbia's Kosovo policy as occupation, not as colonial settlement per se.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Rilindja separated religion from state and sought one secular nation above faith divisions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious freedom was part of Frashëri's vision for the Albanian state, with Jews and Protestants free to worship.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No such ban in Albanian traditions; religious practice is subordinate to the nation.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Secular Albanianism and the 1887 Korçë school were non-confessional; Hoxha went to extremes with state atheism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is Hoxha-era 'state of siege' doctrine, which the nationalism of today does not hold.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Self-determination and referendum calls such as Vetëvendosje's reflect popular-consent legitimacy.

population-transfer.rationale: Albanians themselves suffered expulsions (Chams, Kosovo 1999), so nationalists decry them, though some Albanian actions against Serbs and Roma occurred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nationalists justify force for liberation; the strict libertarian rule is not part of the tradition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The independence story centres on freedom from foreign domination, which loosely fits.

separated-powers.rationale: Vetëvendosje's justice-state pillar stresses checks and balances and judicial independence.

vanguard-party.rationale: Hoxha's party used it but modern nationalists do not.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: No documented position; Albania privatised state housing after 1991.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: No source; the movement ties poverty to ignorance and foreign rule.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Albanian nationalists stress religious unity despite diversity, but fear for ethnic majorities in contested areas.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: No source; modern nationalists use elections.

party-controls-media.rationale: Hoxha's regime did this, and democratic nationalists in Kosovo and Albania reject it today.

party-commands-army.rationale: A communist-era feature rejected by today's nationalists.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Albanians widely see EU integration as the solution to governance problems and Vetëvendosje supports Kosovo's EU membership.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a nationalist issue; Frashëri gave each faith its own leadership.

clerical-rule.rationale: Secular Albanianism rejects clerical rule, and Islam is subsumed under national identity.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: No source; Hoxha-era censorship is rejected today.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Albania and Kosovo seek NATO alignment and US backing; Vetëvendosje aims to join NATO.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No source addresses housing tenure; inferred as a fringe idea outside the nationalist tradition.

people-in-arms.rationale: Kosovo's KLA tradition honours armed citizens but Albania maintains regular forces; no stated position.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Mountain and folk tradition shaped Rilindja romanticism, but no stated claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Albanianism seeks union of Albanian-inhabited lands, and polls show about 80 percent of Albanians in Albania and Kosovo favour union, though most mainstream leaders treat it as rhetoric.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Intellectuals led the Rilindja and the League of Prizren, so adherents revere them.

death-penalty.rationale: Albania and Kosovo abolished the death penalty in line with European norms.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: No documented position; secular schooling tradition suggests opposition.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The ethnic-cultural conception links the nation to Albanians abroad, which implies descent-based membership.

minority-language-support.rationale: Albanians demand Albanian-language schooling in Macedonia and Serbia, and a principled adherent extends it to minorities.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Hoxha's position differs from democratic nationalists.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Vetëvendosje seeks constitutional amendments, but nothing is stated on assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Democratic nationalists reject it, though Hoxha-era claims differ.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Albania and Kosovo rely on NATO and the US; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Kosovo and Albania elect presidents indirectly; no stated nationalist position.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Albanian nationalists defend Kosovo and other Albanian-inhabited lands as the homeland, using the Illyrian narrative to support their claims.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: No documented position; Hoxha broke with the USSR but not on this ground.

collective-defense.rationale: Albania joined NATO and Kosovo's nationalist government seeks to; allied defence is a core security tool.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Albanians regarded Serbian and Yugoslav control of Kosovo as occupation, especially after 1989 revocation of autonomy.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Albania was a secular state and Zog's state promoted Albanianism over religion, while Hoxha went further; nationalists accept the principle in moderate form.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Presidents in Albania and Kosovo play symbolic roles, and Zog's monarchy used the crown as a national symbol.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Albanian nationalists oppose Serbia's use of force against Kosovo's separation, though they would resist Serb secession in the north.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No documented position, though Rilindja leaders sought autonomy within the Ottoman Empire first.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Zog's state was secular and nationalism presented Skanderbeg as a hero, not as a divine ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Albania has used a flat-tax approach, but Vetëvendosje supports progressive taxation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Nationalists in democratic states accept the rule of law; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Skanderbeg, Rugova and Jashari are venerated in public monuments, but the Hoxha cult is repudiated.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist theme not part of nationalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Early twentieth-century debates on land reform exist, but no nationalist doctrine is stated.

refugee-return.rationale: Albanians expelled from Kosovo in 1999 and Chams expelled from Greece are central grievances, so return is demanded.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Greater Albania and 'ethnic Albania' claim lands because Albanians live there, but governments largely disclaim this officially.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Albanianism explicitly puts the nation above religion, and Frashëri guaranteed freedom of worship, which excludes penalising conversion out of a faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Albania and Kosovo are secular and nationalism de-emphasises Islam.

common-currency.rationale: Vetëvendosje has favoured a common currency with Albania.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Albanianism fits, but only for Albanians as a nation, not for language families wider than that.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Albanians in Macedonia and Serbia seek self-governing schools and institutions, and the Rilindja pressed for Albanian schools within the Ottoman state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Albanians in the Preševo Valley and North Macedonia are encouraged to demand rights where they live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The nationalist account explains history through national struggle, not production.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Vetëvendosje stresses checks and balances and judicial independence.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Kosovo has gender quotas, but nationalism does not define a stance.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Pro-EU orientation opposes autarky; Hoxha's autarky is a legacy few defend.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Maoist/Guevarist theme; not part of nationalism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The KLA's guerrilla campaign is honoured by many, though Rugova's nonviolence was the larger movement.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Modern republican nationalists reject titles, though some support the Zogist legacy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Albanian national history, centred on Illyrian descent and Skanderbeg, has been taught as the national story.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Albanians resisted Ottoman, Greek and Slavic domination and their nationalism is anti-tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Interwar and later states promoted national consciousness through schools, and the Rilindja made schooling central to national survival.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Albanian nationalists resent Ottoman rule, though Albanians have close ties with Turkey today.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not held by modern nationalists.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: No source; ethnic equality is a nationalist claim for Albanians abroad.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Vetëvendosje supports constitutional checks and Kosovo's constitution contains rights protections.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Albanians regard the 1878 San Stefano partition and 1913 London settlement, which left half the Albanians outside Albania, as illegitimate impositions.

elective-rulers.rationale: Modern Albanian nationalists accept republican elections over hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: No source; contrasts with Albanian demands for majority self-rule.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to Ottoman, Serbian and Hoxha-era rule is honoured, but no stated doctrine.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Both countries are parliamentary republics and Vetëvendosje has pushed for constitutional order.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nationalism is political mobilisation by definition.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim not part of the nationalist account.

party-own-road.rationale: Hoxha's break with Moscow and Beijing reflected this national path, though today's nationalists do not discuss it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Albania and Kosovo depend on EU and US aid and remittances.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pan-Albanianism asserts that lands lost in 1878 to 1913 should be reunited, though mainstream governments avoid formal demands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Illyrian claims make Albanians indigenous, but Kosovo's constitution protects minorities.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Albania's partisans were communist, but Balli Kombëtar and the SS Skanderbeg division complicate nationalist attitudes.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Divided: Hoxha's regime is condemned, yet WWII collaboration is contested.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments to Skanderbeg and Jashari are defended, but no stated general principle.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Albanian nationalists want Western institutions, EU and NATO, not separate civilizational forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: No stated position; Albanian politics seeks civilian control for NATO entry.

filial-duty.rationale: Kinship and respect for elders in Albanian custom; not stated in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Vetëvendosje's state-development approach might favour it, but no stated stance.

land-use-tenure.rationale: No source supports community ownership of land; inferred from the movement's acceptance of private property.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary systems in both countries; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Albanian is central to the movement, but Albanians themselves demand official language rights in Macedonia and Kosovo grants Serbian official status.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: NATO's support for the KLA was welcomed, but no general principle is stated.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Albanians resent Yugoslav and Soviet-bloc interference, so reject it.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Demographic anxiety exists in contested areas but no stated policy.

non-intervention.rationale: Kosovo's independence depended on NATO intervention, so absolute non-intervention is rejected.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Albanian nationalism has a suspicion of Serbs and Greeks in places but no stated conspiracy narrative.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: No source; inferred from conservative orientation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Vetëvendosje's justice-state anti-corruption programme implies it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Albanian nationalist politics works via parties and movements.

national-law-over-international.rationale: No documented position; Kosovo's constitution incorporates international instruments.

religious-nation.rationale: Albanianism holds that the nation is defined by language and descent, not faith, and Rilindja leaders made the movement secular to unite three religions.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Albanian nationalism resists subordination, though it relies on the US and EU.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: No source; the movement is for a unified state.

defeat-communism.rationale: Albanian nationalists opposed communist rule after 1990, but the Cold War framing is not stated.

religion-illusion.rationale: Hoxha made this a state creed, but modern Albanianism respects religion while subordinating it to the nation.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Early alphabet reform sought a distinct Albanian script, but purism is not a general nationalist demand; Hoxha-era purging is contested.

cooperative-communities.rationale: No source supports small cooperative communities; the movement aims at a unified national state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Albanian nationalists object to Serbian colonisation of Kosovo in the interwar period, so oppose it.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Illyrian continuity narrative is the pillar of claims to Kosovo and other lands, so historical ties are held to ground a stronger claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Albania sheltered Jews in WWII and nationalists celebrate that record, not deny the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Both states have decriminalised it, and nothing in the nationalist sources calls for criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Hoxha's repression is rejected and Kosovo nationalists were themselves the suppressed opposition under Milošević.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Secular Albanianism rejects religious penal law.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Albanians were subjects of empires and oppose colonial rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islam is subsumed in national identity in Kosovo, and nationalism is secular.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: No stated programme; conservative nationalist opinion leans against.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Albanian nationalism spans left and right parties.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Albanian nationalists stress that Albanians are Europeans and that Islam is subordinated to national identity, so they reject incompatibility claims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Secular nationalism grounds authority in the nation and popular will.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Albania and Kosovo ban religious dress in state schools, in line with secular Albanianism.

social-market-economy.rationale: Vetëvendosje's welfare-state programme and EU orientation fit it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Nationalists honour military struggle and Kosovo's government raised military spending.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Albania is in NATO and Kosovo's leading nationalist party seeks it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Zog's monarchy was hereditary but modern nationalists favour republics.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Vetëvendosje's justice-state emphasises rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Albanians campaigned against ethnic discrimination in voting and rights under Yugoslavia.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Albania is religiously mixed and Albanianism builds unity across faiths, so restricting intermarriage is rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: No source; inconsistent with religious unity.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: No documented position; Vetëvendosje's anti-oligarch stance leans yes.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Hoxha's 1967 atheist state is a legacy modern nationalists reject, though it was nationalism's own distortion.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Kosovo's constitution mandates minority seats, and Albanians in Macedonia obtained power sharing in 2001, but some nationalists resist them.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Greater Albania claims exist at the margins, but official Albanian and Kosovar policy disclaims expansion and prefers EU integration.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Kosovo Albanians demand accountability for Serbian forces' killings and expulsions in 1998-99, such as the Jashari family's killing.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nationalism defines the nation by descent and language, and Albanian parties have not campaigned for non-citizen voting, so mild disagreement is inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Housing is not a nationalist issue; the movement spans left and right parties.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: no source records an Albanian nationalist position on intellectual property, and abolition is far outside the mainstream of the movement.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not part of the mainstream strand described; youth and scouting organisations existed but drilled national-service movements were a feature of the Hoxha and interwar regimes this audit excludes.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; Albania and Kosovo are non-nuclear and the question is not part of the nationalist agenda.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Albanian and Kosovar nationalism is Euro-Atlantic and relies on NATO and US forces, so it does not oppose foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: Kosovo Albanians seek recognition of Serbian wartime atrocities as genocide, though the sources do not set out a formal position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by nationalism itself; the left-leaning Vetëvendosje programme favours rewarding labour over capital ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the movement's tradition of armed struggle, from Skanderbeg to the Kosovo war, which treated defence of the nation by force as legitimate.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The movement's founding narrative traces Albanians to Illyrian origins and Skanderbeg in a continuous national history.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is socially conservative in its mainstream, though sources record no explicit view.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socially traditional mainstream of the movement.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: national heroes, from Skanderbeg to Kosovo war dead, are honoured as martyrs, though 'saints' goes beyond what the secular movement claims.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: Albanianism deliberately set religion aside to unite Muslims, Catholics and Orthodox, so it is hostile to a spiritual framing of politics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The programme of unification gathers Albanians into one state, and Pan-Albanianism aims to unite the nation rather than rely on a cultural centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Rilindja developed alphabet, schooling and language before independence in 1912, though the sources do not state it as a doctrine.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; religion is deliberately set aside by the movement.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; religion is deliberately set aside by the movement.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: the nation is defined by language and descent, but the movement also stresses European integration and foreign investment, so it is not strongly majoritarian on the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-Albanianism and Vetëvendosje's call for a unification referendum aim to bring Albanian-inhabited territories into one state; mainstream nationalism treats this as a goal, though less forcefully.

missingStatements.text: A nation should be defined by its shared language and culture rather than by the religions of its members.
missingStatements.rationale: Albanianism, from Vasa's slogan to Frashëri's plan, united Muslims, Catholics and Orthodox on language and descent alone.

missingStatements.text: Peoples living in territories divided among neighbouring states should be able to vote in a referendum on union with their co-nationals.
missingStatements.rationale: Vetëvendosje calls for a unification referendum and surveys show large majorities in both Albania and Kosovo in favour.

notes: Hoxha-era nationalism, the Balli Kombëtar and Pan-Albanian fringe groups would answer differently from the mainstream profile; economic answers split between left (Vetëvendosje) and right (Berisha) nationalists.
